ship.name: Minato Maru
ship.refit: 1998: GMDSS (VHF with DSC, EPIRB, SART, NAVTEX)
ship.yard: Johansson Shipyard (ヨハンソン造船), Innoshima, Seto Inland Sea: hull No. 127, an island ferry like the dozens before her
ship.owner: Minato-chō (the town ferry, a chōei ferī)
ship.type: Passenger ship and vehicle ferry (ryokakusen ken jidōsha tosen), bow ramp only, twin screw
ship.rules: Fictional narrative reference to Japanese inspection and NK class; no actual flag, class or construction approval has been obtained
ship.colours: White superstructure; white hull over red-brown antifouling with a teal sheer band (the ferry company’s colour on the Port Building); teal funnels with the town’s anchor mark

ga.what: Paired aft trim-ballast reservation under the auxiliary room: 2 m3 each. Curved outboard faces follow the hull minus 0.10 m geometric clearance; centreline gap 0.40 m; floor is at least 0.10 m above the loft. Gross 5.3916 m3, 4.8524 m3 after a provisional 10% structure allowance. This replaces the former tank outside the stern hull without crowding the fuel tanks.
ga.why: Trim ballast; final framing and net tank calibration remain to be engineered

ga.what: Steering-gear room: two rudder stocks, rams and tie bar; two 2.2 kW hydraulic power units; the emergency hand pump; the rudder-angle transmitter; the stern-tube oil header tanks; the 5.5 kW emergency fire pump with its own sea suction; a sound-powered telephone and the emergency steering notice
ga.why: Steering, and a fire pump outside the engine room

ga.what: Fresh-water tanks port and starboard, 6 m³ each, the stern tubes between them
ga.why: Water for the taps, the galley and the toilets: 1.5 m³ a day

ga.what: Engine room (batch 6c: from z 8.5, where the counter leaves room for floor plates): the two main engines (x ±1.55, z 9.6–12.0) with their gearboxes aft and turbochargers forward, the shafts aft through the bulkhead; the forward service band of the main engines extends to z 14.0; the two generators are in the auxiliary room; the control booth aft to starboard; fire and general-service pumps, bilge pump, sanitary pump, hydrophore set along the starboard side; the starting-air compressor and two 150 L air bottles against the aft bulkhead to port; the workbench, the fuel purifier and the oily-water separator along the port side; the 1.5 m3 fuel service tank in the forward starboard corner; the sea chests under the plates either side forward; CO₂ nozzles overhead; the watertight door forward on the centreline to the auxiliary machinery room
ga.why: Propulsion and power. Low: 1.9 m clear, and tall men duck under the pipes

ga.what: Engine control booth (2.3 × 1.6 m, soundproofed, glazed towards the engines): the main switchboard on the aft bulkhead, the engine panel and the log desk along her side, the telephone to the bridge
ga.why: Where the chief engineer stands his watch out of the noise

ga.what: Double bottom under the engine room: fuel storage port and starboard (7.5 m3 each), bilge holding (1 m3), sludge (0.3 m3), lubricating oil (0.6 m3): total 16.9 m3 against 18.5526 m3 planning envelope after a 10% structure allowance. Individual tank partitions and calibration remain to be designed.
ga.why: Fuel storage: calculated 9.23 days at the stated duty and 90% usable capacity, excluding idle and weather allowance

ga.what: Shaft space aft of the engine room, over the counter: the two shafts from the gearboxes to the stern tubes, the fresh-water tanks’ fill and air pipes
ga.why: The hull rises aft of z 10.5; the shafts run through here at a slope
ga.unmanned: Reached through a manhole in the engine room’s aft bulkhead, for the shafts’ couplings

ga.what: Auxiliary machinery room, through the watertight sliding door at Fr 28 (kept shut at sea, slid by its hand pump at the door or closed from the bridge): two generator sets relocated to z15.20-16.05 with a 1.00 m centre aisle and at least 1.035 m to side plant; the ballast and bilge manifold and the ballast pump along the starboard side over the tanks they serve, the sewage holding tank (4 m³) and its two discharge pumps to port with the standby pumps in a row before them (fuel transfer No.1 and No.2, hydrophore No.2, sanitary No.2), starting-air compressor No.2 in the aft starboard corner, the sounding pipes to the double bottom, the escape trunk in the forward starboard corner up into casing S
ga.why: The hold forward of the engines was 13.5 m of tanks and voids; a yard puts the auxiliaries that want no watch here, out of the noise, with the ballast valves over their tanks

ga.what: Workshop, through the door at Fr 38: the bench and vice along the forward bulkhead, the JL-400 centre lathe along her side, the pedestal drill, the bench grinder, the welding set, the tool board; a wiped main-bearing shell on the bench, kept for the surveyor
ga.why: Repairs alongside at a bench with room to swing a hammer: the engine room has only the small bench by the ladder

ga.what: Engine store, behind the mesh partition off the workshop: the spares racks (filters, gaskets and seals, injectors, bearings, belts, lamps), two 200 L lubricating-oil drums on their rack with a drip tray, the oily-rag bin, a chain block
ga.why: Spares locked away from the car deck, next to the bench that fits them
ga.unmanned: A store: entered to fetch a part; its one door is the workshop’s, a step from the aux room

ga.what: Double bottom under the auxiliary room, workshop and store: paired trim tanks 2 m3 each at z14.1-15.4; main ballast port and starboard 8 m3 each at z15.6-20.0. These disjoint conformal reservations have 4.8524 and 16.4238 m3 respective planning envelopes after a 10% structure allowance. Unassigned reserve is not additional certified capacity.
ga.why: Heel and trim, with capacities and framing subject to tank design

ga.what: Void between the store and the thruster room: the thruster’s cable and the fore peak’s ballast line run through it; a manhole in the store’s forward bulkhead
ga.why: Kept as a reserve: the ferry office talked of a cold store for the island’s fish and never ordered it

ga.what: Bow-thruster room: the 75 kW motor on its 0.9 m tunnel, the starter cabinet
ga.why: Berthing: it pushes the bow off and on
ga.unmanned: Nobody works in it at sea: it is visited alongside, with the thruster isolated, through its one hatch

ga.what: Fore peak: 6 m³ of ballast, and the two chain lockers under the windlasses
ga.why: Trim, and the anchors’ cables

ga.what: Aft mooring station: the 5.5 kW capstan, two pairs of bitts, closed fairleads, the steering-gear hatch
ga.why: Stern lines

ga.what: Lower lobby (batch 6f), the car deck’s level aft of the lanes, between the casings under a 2.5 m deckhead: the drivers’ waiting benches along the casings, the bicycle rack and the baggage shelf either side of the crew door in the aft bulkhead, a drink machine and the safety plan on the forward bulkhead, lifejacket lockers; the engine-room door (casing P) and its escape (casing S), the feet of both passenger stairs, the foyer from the gangway, the crew door aft to the mooring station, and two 1.1 m sliding fire doors forward onto the lanes
ga.why: Where the drivers wait, the islanders’ bicycles ride, and every way below and above begins: the ways are found, not hunted for

ga.what: Vehicle lanes, 17.4 m: two of 2.75 m, yellow lane lines and numbers, 24 cloverleaf lashing sockets on a 1.25 × 2.5 m grid, wheel-chock racks, six scuppers a side with flaps and freeing ports forward, waterproof tube lights, two exhaust fans, four hydrants, powder extinguishers; the signs “engine off” and “no entry to the car deck at sea”
ga.why: Six cars; a truck on the centreline forward by the loading plan

ga.what: Casing, port, 1.3 m wide: the engine uptake and engine-room supply-fan trunk (z 3–6.25), the engine-room entrance (6.3–7.4, a 1.1 m door) and ladder, passenger stair P (7.4–11.3, 1.2 m clear: its 1.2 m door onto the car deck at 11.35–12.55, the flight rising aft at 48° to the lobby, the crew changing room under it), the foyer at its foot (11.3–13.3) and the gangway passage (13.3–14.7, 1.4 m) with the gangway door and the shore-power box, a fan and a hydrant
ga.why: The engine room’s main way in, a stair up for drivers, and the way aboard from the pier

ga.what: Casing, starboard, 1.3 m wide: uptake trunk (z 3–6), the engine-room escape trunk (6–7), passenger stair S (7.4–12.6, 1.2 m clear, its 1.2 m door at 11.35–12.55; the bosun’s store under its flight: lashings, chocks, ropes, fenders), a fan and a hydrant
ga.why: The engine room’s second way out, the deck stores, the second stair up

ga.what: The way aboard on foot, 1.4 m wide the whole way: the gangway, the gate, the passage through casing P and the foyer aft of it to the foot of stair P, 2.2 m under its deckhead
ga.why: Foot passengers never step onto a car lane

ga.what: Bow house, port: the windlass, the ramp’s hydraulic power pack and its control box, the thruster room’s hatch
ga.why: Anchors and the ramp, worked by the bosun

ga.what: Bow house, starboard: the windlass and the paint store
ga.why: Anchors, and paint kept away from the cabins

ga.what: The bow ramp: hinged at the stem (z 34.3), 4.0 m and a 2.0 m flap that lies flat on the landing, 4.4 m clear; two 100 mm hydraulic cylinders at 14 MPa; two locking pins with limit switches to the “ramp closed and locked” lamp on the bridge; a hand pump
ga.why: Lowered, 5° to the quay; raised, it closes the bow 4 m high

ga.what: Open deck: benches for 22 under an awning, one liferaft (port, aft), the rescue boat and its davit (starboard, aft), the stern flagstaff, two lifebuoys, the sign for muster station B
ga.why: Fresh air, the view, and where people embark the liferafts

ga.what: Lobby, the deckhouse’s full breadth: the stair heads P and S in its wings; the purser’s window (S: ticket rack, cash box, punch, PA microphone, first-aid kit, lost property); the kiosk (P counter); the vending corner (two drink machines and a hot-water dispenser for cup noodles); timetable and fare boards; the capacity sign and the ship’s certificate; an ashtray stand by the aft door
ga.why: Tickets and snacks; everyone passes through

ga.what: Toilets: men’s to port (a WC, two urinals, a basin), women’s to starboard (two WCs, a basin); sea-water flushing
Carpet room, raised 0.3 m: carpet, a rack of cushions and blankets, the shoe shelf at the step, a television on a bracket, life-jacket lockers; 36 places
ga.why: Lie down for twenty-two minutes, as everyone does

ga.what: Seated saloon: a cross passage at its aft end to the side doors (z 16.5–17.6), then 42 moquette seats in seven rows of three each side at 0.85 m, windows forward over the car deck and the sea, life-jacket lockers, the sign for muster station A
ga.why: The forward view

ga.what: Side walkway, port, 0.7 m: rails, two liferafts in cradles outboard of the rail, a hydrant, and the ladder up to the bridge wing at its forward end (z 17.6–19.5)
ga.why: Crew and escape

ga.what: Side walkway, starboard, 0.7 m: rails, two liferafts in cradles outboard of the rail, a hydrant, and the ladder up to the bridge wing at its forward end (z 17.6–19.5)
ga.why: Crew and escape

ga.what: Emergency-generator room: the 40 kVA emergency generator, the emergency switchboard, the 24 V batteries and their chargers, a 60 L day tank, louvres
ga.why: Power when the main board is dead; its door opens to the open deck only

ga.what: CO₂ room and fire-control station: four 45 kg CO₂ bottles, the release cabinet, the remote fan stops and fuel quick-closing valves, two firemen’s outfits
ga.why: Fire in the engine room is fought from outside it; its door opens to the open deck only

ga.what: Crew cabin, two berths: the bosun and the oiler; bunk beds, lockers, a fold-down desk
Chief officer’s cabin
Deckhand’s cabin
ga.why: On her weeks aboard

ga.what: Crew WC and shower
Mess room: a table for six, a television, a kettle, the duty board and the muster list
ga.why: Where the crew eat and the watch is handed over

ga.what: Galley: a three-plate range, the rice cooker, a fridge-freezer, a sink, a hood, the provision locker, a hatch to the mess
ga.why: The cook’s; the kiosk’s hot water too

ga.what: Chief engineer’s cabin
Master’s cabin: a desk, a bunk, the ship’s papers and the safe
The crew’s corridor down the middle, from their own door aft onto the bridge deck’s platform (they come up the open deck’s ladders) to the wheelhouse
ga.why: The crew’s way to their rooms and to the bridge, apart from the passengers

ga.what: Wheelhouse: the steering stand (wheel, non-follow-up lever, autopilot); two engine levers and the thruster lever at the centre and on both wing consoles; the radar; the magnetic compass periscope; VHF with DSC; the ship’s telephone; the NAVTEX printer; the echo sounder; the GPS display; the chart table with its drawers and red lamp; the navigation-light panel; the fire panel; the PA and general alarm; the ramp lamps; the whistle button; the searchlight control; the wipers; a clock, a barometer, an inclinometer; the log desk; the master’s high chair
ga.why: She is conned from here and from the wings

ga.what: Bridge wing, port, open: a wing console with the engine and thruster levers, the port sidelight at its end
ga.why: Berthing port side to

ga.what: Bridge wing, starboard, open: a wing console, the starboard sidelight at its end, the float-free EPIRB
ga.why: Berthing starboard side to

ga.what: Compass deck: the standard magnetic compass, the mast with the radar scanner on its platform, the masthead light at 15 m, the all-round lights, the whistle, the VHF and GPS antennas, the searchlight, the company flag
ga.why: What she sees and is seen by

ga.what: Funnel, port: the port main engine’s and No.1 generator’s exhausts
ga.why: Twin funnels at the open deck’s forward corners, clear of the bridge-deck house

ga.what: Funnel, starboard: the starboard main engine’s and No.2 generator’s exhausts

mains.kind: Four-stroke medium-speed marine diesel, six in line, turbocharged and intercooled
mains.start: Compressed air at 2.94 MPa (30 kgf/cm²) from two 150 L bottles
mains.driven: Each engine drives its own lubricating-oil, jacket-water and sea-water pumps: they run when the engine runs, with or without electricity, so a blackout does not stop the propellers

gears.kind: Reverse-reduction gearbox with hydraulic multi-disc ahead and astern clutches; bridge control from the wheelhouse and both wings, emergency control in the engine room

shafts.kind: Oil-lubricated stern tubes with lip seals; header tanks in the steering-gear room

propellers.why: Fixed pitch, because the gears reverse: the small ferry’s choice of the period

steering.kind: Electro-hydraulic, two power units: one at sea, both in narrow water
steering.hardOver: 35° one side to 30° the other in under 28 s
steering.emergency: No.2 is fed from the emergency switchboard; a hand pump and a telephone to the bridge

bowThruster.interlock: May start only with two generators on the board

bilge.why: The rule asks for 25 + 1.68·√(L(B+D)) millimetres: 57 for her

co2.why: Provisional inventory screen only: 180 kg carried against an assumed 190 m3 protected volume. Actual fire boundaries, ducts, protected volumes, nozzle distribution and release interlocks require engineered verification

freshWater.why: Filled every fifth morning from Mr Chinen’s water lorry

ramp.why: One pump runs and one stands by; a hand pump if both fail

electrics.distribution: 440 V three-phase three-wire, insulated from earth (earth lamps and an insulation meter on the board)

generators.trips: over-current, short-time, under-voltage and reverse power (about 10 %)

emergency.why: Provisional continuous capacity only. Emergency fire-pump starting and voltage recovery require generator/AVR/governor transient validation; current comparison alone does not prove performance.

shore.transformer: 50 kVA 200/440 V in the quay kiosk at Minato
shore.interlock: Shore power and the generators never run together: the shore breaker and the generators’ breakers are interlocked

boards.MSB: Main switchboard, in the engine control booth: DG1, synchronising (synchroscope, lamps, two kW meters, Hz, V, A, three earth lamps, insulation meter), DG2, two 440 V feeder panels, shore
boards.LB: 105 V lighting board, fed through one of the two 30 kVA transformers
boards.ESB: Emergency switchboard, 440 V and 105 V sections, in the emergency-generator room: fed from the main board through a bus-tie, and from the emergency generator when the main board is dead

preferenceTrip.why: Before a generator is overloaded the board sheds what can wait: stage 1 the saloon air conditioning, the kiosk and the vending machines; stage 2 the galley and the water heater
